subject: Computer Networking
title: Tracking Pixels and Privacy
description: A fast breakdown of Tracking Pixels and Privacy for builders.

hook.text: Did they open your email? A tiny invisible image tells the sender exactly when and where you read it.

buildup.text: A tracking pixel is a 1×1 transparent image hosted on the sender's server. Loading it logs the open event.

discovery.text: The log captures your IP, device type, OS, and exact time. All from opening one email.

twist.text: Apple Mail Privacy Protection now pre-fetches all images. The sender sees an open even if you never read it.

climax.text: Hey.com blocks all trackers by default and shows which emails tried to spy on you. A privacy revolt.

punchline.text: Tracking pixels spy silently. Privacy tools are fighting back.

quiz.question: How does Apple Mail Privacy Protection defeat tracking pixels?
options: It pre-fetches all images so real open data is hidden
It blocks all emails containing images
It converts images to text descriptions

details.summary: Tracking pixels are tiny invisible images embedded in emails that notify the sender when the email is opened. They reveal whether, when, where, and on what device you read the message. Email privacy features that block external images are specifically designed to defeat tracking pixels.
details.whyItMatters: Every marketing email you open likely reports back to the sender. Understanding tracking pixels explains why email privacy settings exist and why they matter.
takeaways: Tracking pixels are invisible images that report email opens
They reveal open time, location, and device information
Blocking external images defeats most tracking pixels

faq.question: How do tracking pixels work technically?
faq.answer: The email contains an image tag pointing to a unique URL on the sender's server. When your email client loads the image, the server logs the request including your IP address, user agent, and timestamp. The image is typically a 1x1 transparent pixel, invisible to you.

faq.question: How can you protect yourself from email tracking?
faq.answer: Disable automatic image loading in your email client. Use Apple Mail Privacy Protection or similar features that pre-fetch images through a proxy. Use email clients that block tracking by default. Be aware that any email with external images can track your reading behavior.
